_note: Adversarial conformance corpus. Every case is a receipt a verifier must refuse. All reference implementations run this and must agree — see tests/run_conformance_cases.py and tests/run_conformance_cases.mjs.

cases.name: bundle_smuggling
cases.why: A forged receipt carrying one genuine receipt printed VERIFIED and exited 0; the unsigned top-level `receipts` array decided what got verified. Pinning did not help.

cases.name: nfd_entity_evasion
cases.why: A banned entity spelled in NFD evaded the predicate while canonicalizing to byte-identical signed input — the signed bytes did not determine the verdict. Now refused earlier: identity names are ASCII, so no two spellings of one name exist.

cases.name: version_bypass_latest
cases.why: `<2.0` was satisfied by 'latest' because non-numeric components parsed as 0.

cases.name: version_bypass_main
cases.why: `<2.0` was satisfied by 'main' because non-numeric components parsed as 0.

cases.name: version_bypass_v3.0
cases.why: `<2.0` was satisfied by 'v3.0' because non-numeric components parsed as 0.

cases.name: version_bypass_empty
cases.why: `<2.0` was satisfied by '' because non-numeric components parsed as 0.

cases.name: enum_fail_open_status_ACTIVE
cases.why: beliefs[0].status='ACTIVE' silently disabled the constraint and verified as ALLOW.

cases.name: enum_fail_open_rule_EXCLUDES
cases.why: beliefs[0].rule='EXCLUDES' silently disabled the constraint and verified as ALLOW.

cases.name: enum_fail_open_rule_excludes
cases.why: beliefs[0].rule='excludes ' silently disabled the constraint and verified as ALLOW.

cases.name: enum_fail_open_source_kind_DETERMINISTIC
cases.why: beliefs[0].source_kind='DETERMINISTIC' silently disabled the constraint and verified as ALLOW.

cases.name: enum_fail_open_belief_class_certified
cases.why: beliefs[0].belief_class='certified' silently disabled the constraint and verified as ALLOW.

cases.name: belief_missing_entity
cases.why: An active deterministic constraint without 'entity' was skipped (Python) or crashed (JS) instead of failing.

cases.name: belief_missing_rule
cases.why: An active deterministic constraint without 'rule' was skipped (Python) or crashed (JS) instead of failing.

cases.name: belief_missing_belief_id
cases.why: An active deterministic constraint without 'belief_id' was skipped (Python) or crashed (JS) instead of failing.

cases.name: belief_equals_missing_value
cases.why: An `equals` constraint without a value cannot be evaluated.

cases.name: asserts_not_object
cases.why: action.asserts as a string crashed the predicate.

cases.name: beliefs_not_list
cases.why: beliefs as a string iterated characters and crashed.

cases.name: belief_not_object
cases.why: A non-object belief entry crashed .get().

cases.name: signature_not_object
cases.why: A string signature block crashed .get(); the correct answer is an invalid signature.

cases.name: action_not_object
cases.why: A string action crashed the binding check.

cases.name: assert_value_not_string
cases.why: Non-string assert values made Python recompute HALT and JS recompute ALLOW.

cases.name: integer_above_2_53
cases.why: Integers above 2**53 collapsed to a neighbour in JS, so a tampered body kept a colliding hash in one language and not the other.

cases.name: non_integral_number
cases.why: Python repr and ECMAScript ToString share no float grammar (1e21, 1e16, 1e-6 all differed).

cases.name: small_order_key_identity
cases.why: The canonical identity point. One constant signature block verified EVERY receipt in all three implementations until 534dfb6.

cases.name: small_order_key_sign_bit
cases.why: Ed25519 stores the x-coordinate's sign in the high bit of byte 31, so the identity point has a second spelling that OpenSSL and WebCrypto both accept. The blacklist compared all 32 bytes and missed it; libsodium masks s[31] & 127 first.

cases.name: small_order_key_p_plus_1
cases.why: p+1 also decodes to the identity point.

cases.name: post_state_root_null_on_allow
cases.why: The schema requires post_state_root == pre_state_root on ALLOW.

cases.name: action_binding_tool_mismatch
cases.why: The binding named a different tool than the action it claims to bind.

cases.name: deep_nesting
cases.why: 300 levels of nesting raised RecursionError in Python and returned a verdict in JS.

cases.name: duplicate_key_after_nfc
cases.why: Two assert keys identical after NFC are ambiguous; canonical JSON would emit a duplicate.

cases.name: identity_entity_non_ascii
cases.why: NFC is bound to the runtime's Unicode version (CPython 15.0 vs Node 16.0; 20 code points compose in one and not the other), so a decomposed spelling evaded the gate in one implementation and not the other. Identity names are ASCII.

cases.name: identity_assert_key_non_ascii
cases.why: Same class, on the assert side.

cases.name: status_explicit_null
cases.why: beliefs[0].status = null: Python's dict.get(k, default) and JavaScript's `?? default` disagree on an explicit null, so one verifier read the constraint as present-and-valid and the other rejected the receipt. Schema requires a string.

cases.name: source_kind_explicit_null
cases.why: beliefs[0].source_kind = null: Python's dict.get(k, default) and JavaScript's `?? default` disagree on an explicit null, so one verifier read the constraint as present-and-valid and the other rejected the receipt. Schema requires a string.

cases.name: belief_class_explicit_null
cases.why: beliefs[0].belief_class = null: Python's dict.get(k, default) and JavaScript's `?? default` disagree on an explicit null, so one verifier read the constraint as present-and-valid and the other rejected the receipt. Schema requires a string.

cases.name: version_leading_whitespace
cases.why: Python's str.strip and ECMAScript's String.trim remove different whitespace sets, flipping ALLOW/HALT on the same bytes.

cases.name: base64_padded_junk
cases.why: Node, CPython and WebCrypto accepted three different sets of malformed base64.

cases.name: null_document
cases.why: Both JS verifiers threw an uncaught TypeError on JSON null instead of returning a verdict; Python returned FAILED. A crash is not a verdict.

cases.name: compatible_release_single_component
cases.why: `~=2` has no upper bound to enforce — it degenerated into >=2, so the pin never gated. PEP 440 requires at least two components.

cases.name: certified_label_on_nl_extracted_belief
cases.why: A prose-extracted belief wearing the word CERTIFIED. It never gated (the recompute keys on source_kind) but the signed label read CERTIFIED to any human or dashboard — trust in the producer creeping back into a format whose claim is that you need not trust the producer.

cases.name: best_effort_label_on_deterministic_belief
cases.why: The mirror case: a belief that DOES gate while labelled advisory. Pinning only the other direction would have left this half of the class reachable.

cases.name: belief_class_absent
cases.why: er1.schema.json lists belief_class in `required` for every constraint, but the verifier checked it only `if present` — looser than the schema it publishes.

cases.name: unpinned_declared_gap_recomputes
cases.why: Control for the declaration rule: unpinned install, gap correctly declared — every predicate check must pass and the ONLY failure is the missing signature, proving the cases below fail for their own stated reason. (Signed positives live in the golden vectors.) Under 1.0.0 this receipt — the honest producer's actual output — was refused as malformed.

unevaluated_constraints.reason: no version pinned in the action; the constraint was not evaluated

cases.name: phantom_declaration
cases.why: The declaration names an entity with no unevaluable constraint. An over-declaration asserts a check was skipped that actually ran (or never existed) — accepting it would let a producer blanket-declare everything and turn the field into noise.

cases.name: phantom_declaration_evaluable
cases.why: The declared entity exists but its constraint WAS evaluable (version pinned): the gap did not exist, so the declaration is false and the receipt is refused. The declared set must equal recomputation in both directions.

unevaluated_constraints.reason: no version pinned in the action; the constraint was not evaluated

cases.name: unevaluated_declaration_not_array
cases.why: The field carries semantics as of 1.0.1, so an unreadable shape fails closed instead of being skipped — a check that reports instead of gating is how every prior bypass began.

cases.name: unevaluated_entry_not_object
cases.why: Same class, one level down.

cases.name: unevaluated_entry_constraint_null
cases.why: Same class: an explicit null is not a declaration.

cases.name: unevaluated_entry_reason_not_string
cases.why: The reason is prose and its content is not verified, but its TYPE is — a non-string smuggled into a signed field must not canonicalize into something two languages read differently.

cases.name: declared_gap_on_malformed_rule
cases.why: An ASSERTED rule whose own version does not parse is MALFORMED, and that refusal wins: the verdict recompute reaches the broken rule before the declaration is even examined. A malformed rule cannot be laundered into an ALLOW by declaring it.

cases.name: declared_gap_on_unasserted_malformed_rule
cases.why: The phantom path for a malformed rule: when its entity is NOT asserted, the broken rule is never evaluated (same as 1.0.0's short-circuit scope) — but declaring it as a gap is still phantom, because recomputation never classifies a malformed rule as unevaluable.

cases.name: compat_single_component_not_declarable
cases.why: `~=2` is invalid per PEP 440 regardless of the proposed version (checked before the proposed version is looked at), and that refusal wins over any declaration. Declaring it as a coverage gap must not launder a malformed rule into an ALLOW — a verifier that drops the arity check turns this into a declarable gap and verifies, which is what this case exists to catch.

cases.name: unpinned_bare_pin_recomputes_halt
cases.why: The bare pin is the STRICT spelling — 'the action must pin this exact version' — and an unpinned action VIOLATES it (string inequality, exactly as 1.0.0 evaluated it). It is never a declarable gap: the first 1.0.1 draft reclassified this cell and an external reviewer showed that flipped a published protective refusal into a verifying ALLOW. `==X` is the gap-declarable spelling.

cases.name: bare_pin_declared_is_phantom
cases.why: Declaring the bare-pin cell as a gap must be phantom — recomputation classifies only OPERATOR constraints as unevaluable. This is the case that catches a verifier drifting back to the first draft's reclassification.

cases.name: phantom_declaration_on_halt
cases.why: The undeclared-gap rule is ALLOW-only, but the PHANTOM rule holds under both verdicts: a HALT receipt asserting a gap that recomputation cannot find is still lying about what was checked.

cases.name: legacy_halt_undeclared_trailing_gap_is_tolerated
cases.why: Control for the ALLOW-only asymmetry, from an external reviewer's counterexample: a 1.0.0-era HALT receipt whose short-circuited conflict left a trailing unpinned constraint unevaluated — and, being pre-1.0.1, undeclared. 1.0.0 VERIFIED this shape, so 1.0.1 must too: every predicate check passes and the ONLY failure is the missing signature. (The signed twin lives in the golden vectors.) An unevaluable constraint can never BE the conflict, so nothing launders through a refusal.

cases.name: neq_satisfied_recomputes_allow
cases.why: 2.5 satisfies !=2.0, so the recorded HALT must recompute as ALLOW. 1.0.0 had no `!=` operator and string-compared the whole expression, agreeing with this wrong verdict — an operator the producer's requirements extractor accepts, mis-evaluated as a bare string.

cases.name: spaced_operator_target_recomputes
cases.why: `>= 2.0` is how humans write pins; the U+0020 around the version is lexed (by hand — strip()/trim() remove different whitespace sets). 1.0 violates it, so the recorded ALLOW must recompute as HALT. Under 1.0.0 this ordinary constraint was malformed.

cases.name: tab_after_operator_is_malformed
cases.why: ONLY U+0020 is blessed. A tab after the operator is not lexed — widening the accepted whitespace is exactly how the two languages' strip()/trim() divergence gets back in.

cases.name: well_formed_halt_recomputes
cases.why: Control: unsigned, so it must fail on the SIGNATURE only — proving the corpus's other cases fail for their own stated reason and the predicate still works.
